gaps.lead: 'Don't touch the paintings in this room,' the guide warned us.
gaps.sentence: The guide warned ___ the paintings in that room.
gaps.explanation: Negative commands are reported with warned + object + not to + infinitive.

gaps.lead: The number of students is rising.
gaps.sentence: There is ___ the number of students.
gaps.explanation: 'Is rising' becomes the noun: 'an increase in'.

gaps.lead: The match officials postponed the fixture because of the storm.
gaps.sentence: The fixture ___ because of the storm.
gaps.explanation: 'Postpone' = 'put off'; in the passive: the fixture was put off.

gaps.lead: My advice is to check the contract twice before signing.
gaps.sentence: You ___ the contract twice before signing.
gaps.explanation: had better + infinitive without 'to' = strong advice.

gaps.lead: I want you to stop tapping your pen while I am working.
gaps.sentence: I ___ tapping your pen while I am working.
gaps.explanation: 'I want you to stop' becomes 'I wish you would stop' — wish + would for irritation.

gaps.lead: Everyone thought the concert was excellent.
gaps.explanation: 'Everyone thought it excellent' → 'made an excellent impression on everyone'.

gaps.lead: I have never read such a gripping novel.
gaps.sentence: This is ___ I have ever read.
gaps.explanation: 'Never read such a gripping novel' = 'the most gripping novel I have ever read'.

gaps.lead: I think learning to use a typewriter is a waste of time.
gaps.sentence: I can't ___ how to use a typewriter.
gaps.explanation: 'A waste of time' becomes 'can't see the point in/of doing it'.
